title: Four Friends Lower the Paralytic Through the Roof
text:
In the Gospel of Mark, Jesus came back to Capernaum, and word spread that he was at home. So many people gathered that the house was full and there was no room left, not even around the door. He was speaking to them.

Four men arrived carrying a friend who was paralyzed, lying on a mat. They could not get near Jesus because of the crowd. So they climbed onto the flat roof. They dug through the roof above the place where Jesus was, made an opening, and lowered the mat with the paralyzed man on it down into the room.

When Jesus saw their faith, Mark says, he said to the paralyzed man that his sins were forgiven. Some scribes who were sitting there grumbled to themselves that only God could forgive sins. Jesus asked them which was easier, to say "your sins are forgiven" or to say "get up, take your mat and walk." To show them, he told the man to get up, pick up his mat and go home.

The man got up, picked up his mat at once and walked out in front of them all. The crowd was amazed and praised God, saying they had never seen anything like it.
lesson: Friends who share the weight of a burden can find a way through when the front door is blocked. Sometimes helping means carrying someone and refusing to give up.
people: Jesus, a paralyzed man, his four friends, the scribes
